standard: Pakistan Halal Authority Act 2016; PSQCA PS 3733:2010 and PS 4992:2010
import_recognition: Accredited certification bodies must be recognised by the Government of Pakistan
notes: The Act bars marketing anything as halal without the Authority's logo, so certification is mandatory for a halal claim. No route for cell-based food found. Statute text not read. phase1/ adds that the Act's nationwide scope covers imports, exports and interprovincial halal trade, some sections have deferred commencement, and the provincial food authority and product classification route are unresolved.

standard: No unifying halal law; FSSAI licence for food
import_recognition: Halal certificate not needed for trade permission, but required by GCC, Malaysia, Indonesia and other OIC markets for exports
notes: Corrected 30 Sep 2026. Earlier value was none_found. FSSAI's 2017 regulations (2022 compendium) require prior approval for non-specified foods, and Form I covers novel foods and technologies. This is a general route; no cultivated-chicken approval is documented. i-CAS from PLAN.md not sourced. See phase1/review.md.

body: Saudi Food and Drug Authority, Saudi Halal Center
import_recognition: Importers need halal and halal-shipment certificates from bodies recognised by the Saudi Halal Center
notes: Corrected 30 Sep 2026. Earlier value was none_found. The SFDA novel-food requirements expressly include food from animal cell or tissue culture and refer to halal sources and the GSO halal standard; a December 2025 SFDA announcement confirms a dedicated route. The official English documents show inconsistent regulation numbers (513/2020, 5031:2020, 5013), so the controlling version needs confirming from the Arabic. No named cultivated-chicken authorisation is established; HS-009's statement that none had been issued still stands. See phase1/review.md.

body: Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology (MoIAT)
import_recognition: Food sold or labelled halal must be certified by a body accredited by EIAC or GAC
notes: From search summaries of MoIAT pages; not opened. Novel-food route not searched. phase1/ found a WAM announcement of 24 Oct 2025 about an Abu Dhabi novel-food framework; its body describes development of a framework, so no completed route is shown, and it is emirate-level. The federal route and the operative ADAFSA instrument are still to be found. MoIAT calls the Halal National Mark optional, which does not make every certificate optional.
JAKIM issued a cultivated-meat fatwa (FT-005). Certification rules not checked in this pass.

body: BPJPH, with an MUI fatwa and an accredited halal inspection body
import_recognition: Imported food, drink and slaughter products must be certified by 17 October 2026 per a 2026 USDA report
notes: No MUI or BPJPH position on cultivated meat found in this pass. Report summary read from search results. phase1/ adds BPJPH Decree 221/2025 (15 Sep 2025, in force three months later), which sets foreign-certificate registration through SIHALAL. It is halal administration, not a cultivated-food route.

Corrected 30 Sep 2026. Earlier value was unknown. The food route is SFA premarket approval for novel foods; the 14 Aug 2026 approved list names Eat Just serum-containing chicken (26 Nov 2020), serum-free chicken (11 Jan 2023) and Vital Meat embryonic stem-cell biomass (17 Oct 2025). The halal route is separate: MUIS said in Feb 2024 it would develop certification guidelines, and its fuller monograph says they still need developing. No matching halal certificate was found. See phase1/review.md.
